questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: At chemical equilibrium in a closed system, which statement is correct?
options: Forward and reverse rates are equal
Reactant and product concentrations are equal
questions.explanation: Both reactions continue at equal rates. Constant concentration does not mean equal concentration.
questions.hint: Distinguish a reaction rate from a concentration.

misconceptions.0: Conceptual: equilibrium may be treated as static
misconceptions.2: Conceptual: constant and equal concentrations may be confused

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: At equilibrium, the forward rate is 0.04 mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹. What is the reverse rate?
questions.explanation: At equilibrium forward and reverse rates are equal, so the reverse rate is 0.04 mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹.
questions.hint: Apply the defining condition of dynamic equilibrium.

misconceptions.0: Conceptual: reverse reaction may be assumed to stop
misconceptions.3: Recall: equilibrium rate condition may need checking

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: For N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), which is Kc?
questions.explanation: Products form the numerator; coefficients become powers: [NH₃]²/([N₂][H₂]³).
questions.hint: Use coefficients as powers, not multipliers.

misconceptions.0: Procedural: stoichiometric powers may be missing
misconceptions.2: Procedural: numerator and denominator may be reversed
misconceptions.3: Procedural: coefficients may be used as multipliers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: For CaCO₃(s) ⇌ CaO(s) + CO₂(g), which is Kc?
questions.explanation: Activities of pure solids are unity; only the gaseous CO₂ concentration remains.
questions.hint: Which substances have unit activity?

misconceptions.0: Conceptual: pure solids may be included in the expression
misconceptions.2: Procedural: product term may be inverted

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: For A ⇌ B, equilibrium [A] = 0.20 M and [B] = 0.60 M. Calculate Kc.
questions.explanation: For this 1:1 reaction, Kc = [B]/[A] = 0.60/0.20 = 3. The equilibrium ratio favors products.
questions.hint: Put the product concentration above the reactant concentration.

misconceptions.0: Procedural: equilibrium ratio may be inverted
misconceptions.1: Procedural: concentrations may be multiplied instead of divided

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: If Kc for A ⇌ B is 4, what is Kc for B ⇌ A at the same temperature?
questions.explanation: Reversing a reaction inverts its equilibrium constant: 1/4 = 0.25.
questions.hint: Write both equilibrium expressions.

misconceptions.0: Conceptual: reversal may be assumed to leave K unchanged
misconceptions.1: Procedural: reversing may be confused with changing the sign

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: For H₂ + I₂ ⇌ 2HI, Kc = 9. What is Kc for ½H₂ + ½I₂ ⇌ HI?
questions.explanation: Multiplying coefficients by ½ raises Kc to the power ½. √9 = 3.
questions.hint: Scaling a reaction changes the powers in its expression.

misconceptions.1: Procedural: K may be scaled linearly
misconceptions.3: Procedural: scaling exponent may be reversed

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: For N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), what is Δn?
questions.explanation: Δn = 2 − (1 + 3) = −2. Count gaseous coefficients only.
questions.hint: Subtract reactant gas coefficients from product gas coefficients.

misconceptions.0: Procedural: gas mole difference may have its sign reversed
misconceptions.3: Conceptual: total gaseous coefficients may replace the difference

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: For H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g), how are Kp and Kc related?
questions.explanation: Δn = 2 − 2 = 0, so (RT)^0 = 1 and Kp = Kc.
questions.hint: Calculate Δn first.

misconceptions.3: Procedural: product moles alone may be used for Δn

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: Adding a catalyst to an equilibrium mixture will:
questions.explanation: A catalyst accelerates both directions and does not change Kc or equilibrium composition.
questions.hint: Separate speed of reaching equilibrium from equilibrium position.

misconceptions.0: Conceptual: rate and equilibrium constant may be confused
misconceptions.1: Conceptual: a catalyst may be assumed to favor products

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: For N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), compressing the mixture at constant temperature shifts equilibrium:
options: Neither way, because Kc is constant
Only if a catalyst is present
questions.explanation: Higher pressure favors the side with fewer gas moles: 2 on the product side versus 4 on the reactant side. Kc remains constant.
questions.hint: Count the gas coefficients on each side.

misconceptions.1: Procedural: pressure shift direction may be reversed
misconceptions.2: Conceptual: constant K may be confused with constant composition

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: For an exothermic forward reaction, increasing temperature will:
questions.explanation: Heating favors the endothermic reverse direction, lowering the equilibrium product-to-reactant ratio and K.
questions.hint: Treat heat as a product for an exothermic reaction.

misconceptions.0: Conceptual: faster reaction may be confused with larger equilibrium constant
misconceptions.2: Recall: temperature dependence of K may be missed

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.prompt: Which equation is quadratic in x?
questions.explanation: The highest remaining power must be 2 with nonzero coefficient. In the last option the x² terms cancel.
questions.hint: Simplify before identifying the degree.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.prompt: Write x(x + 3) = 10 in standard form. What is c?
questions.explanation: Expanding and rearranging gives x² + 3x − 10 = 0, so c = −10.
questions.hint: Move the constant to the left side.

misconceptions.0: Procedural: sign may not change when rearranging
misconceptions.1: Recall: b and c may be confused

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.prompt: Find the roots of x² − 5x + 6 = 0.
questions.explanation: x² − 5x + 6 = (x − 2)(x − 3); each factor can be zero, so x = 2 or 3.
questions.hint: Find numbers whose product is 6 and sum is −5.

misconceptions.0: Procedural: factor signs may be confused with root signs
misconceptions.2: Procedural: only the product may have been checked

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.prompt: Solve 2x² − 8x = 0.
questions.explanation: Factor 2x(x − 4) = 0. Both x = 0 and x = 4 are solutions. Dividing by x would discard x = 0.
questions.hint: Factor instead of dividing by x.

misconceptions.0: Procedural: dividing by x may discard the zero root

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.prompt: What is the discriminant of x² − 6x + 9 = 0?
questions.hint: Square the whole coefficient b, including its sign.

misconceptions.0: Procedural: subtraction in D may become addition
misconceptions.3: Calculation: squaring a negative coefficient may be incorrect

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.prompt: How many real roots does 2x² + 3x + 5 = 0 have?
questions.explanation: D = 9 − 40 = −31 < 0; there are no real roots.
questions.hint: Use the sign of b² − 4ac.

misconceptions.0: Conceptual: all quadratics may be assumed to have real roots
misconceptions.1: Recall: D < 0 may be confused with D = 0

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.prompt: For x² + kx + 16 = 0 to have equal real roots, k must be:
questions.explanation: Equal roots require D = k² − 64 = 0, so k² = 64 and k = ±8.
questions.hint: Remember both square roots when solving for k.

misconceptions.0: Procedural: negative solution may be discarded
misconceptions.1: Procedural: positive solution may be discarded

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.prompt: Which is the correct formula for roots of ax² + bx + c = 0?
questions.explanation: The numerator is −b ± √(b² − 4ac), all divided by 2a.
questions.hint: Check the sign before b, the discriminant and the entire denominator.

misconceptions.0: Recall: leading negative sign may be missing
misconceptions.3: Recall: discriminant sign may be incorrect

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.prompt: The roots of 2x² + x − 3 = 0 are:
questions.hint: Use a = 2, b = 1 and c = −3.

misconceptions.1: Procedural: sign of −b may be reversed

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.prompt: A rectangle has width x cm and length (x + 3) cm. Its area is 40 cm². Find its width.
questions.explanation: x(x + 3) = 40 gives (x + 8)(x − 5) = 0. The positive width is 5 cm.
questions.hint: Form an area equation, then reject an invalid length.

misconceptions.1: Misinterpretation: length may be given instead of width
misconceptions.2: Misinterpretation: a negative length may be accepted

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.prompt: The product of two consecutive positive integers is 72. Find the smaller integer.
questions.explanation: Let the smaller integer be x: x(x + 1) = 72. (x + 9)(x − 8) = 0; positivity gives x = 8.
questions.hint: Consecutive integers can be written x and x + 1.

misconceptions.0: Misinterpretation: larger integer may be reported
misconceptions.2: Misinterpretation: positivity constraint may be ignored

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.prompt: Enter the positive root of x² − 2x − 8 = 0.
questions.explanation: (x − 4)(x + 2) = 0 gives 4 and −2. The requested positive root is 4.
questions.hint: Factor using numbers with product −8 and sum −2.

skills.name: Dynamic equilibrium
skills.subject: Chemistry
skills.description: At equilibrium, forward and reverse reaction rates are equal. Reactions continue and concentrations stay constant.

skills.name: Law of mass action
skills.subject: Chemistry
skills.description: In the equilibrium expression, each concentration is raised to its stoichiometric coefficient. Pure solids and liquids have unit activity.

skills.name: Equilibrium constant Kc
skills.subject: Chemistry
skills.description: Kc is the ratio of product to reactant concentration terms at equilibrium. Its value depends on temperature.

skills.name: Kp and gaseous moles
skills.subject: Chemistry
skills.description: Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn, where Δn is gaseous product coefficients minus gaseous reactant coefficients.

skills.name: Le Chatelier’s principle
skills.subject: Chemistry
skills.description: A system shifts to oppose a concentration, pressure or temperature change. A catalyst changes the rate of reaching equilibrium, not its position.

skills.name: Standard quadratic form
skills.subject: Mathematics
skills.description: A quadratic has the form ax² + bx + c = 0, with a ≠ 0. Move every term to one side before identifying coefficients.

skills.name: Factorisation
skills.subject: Mathematics
skills.description: Write the quadratic as a product equal to zero. At least one factor must be zero; solve both factors.

skills.name: Discriminant
skills.subject: Mathematics
skills.description: D = b² − 4ac. D > 0 means two distinct real roots; D = 0 means equal real roots; D < 0 means no real roots.

skills.name: Quadratic formula
skills.subject: Mathematics
skills.description: For ax² + bx + c = 0, x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac))/(2a). Keep the entire numerator over 2a.

skills.name: Word problems
skills.subject: Mathematics
skills.description: Define the variable, form a quadratic and check roots against the context. Lengths and counts must be valid.
